blindSummary:
Trans visitors to this country face extreme risk. A 2008 penal code criminalises same-sex conduct (up to 14 years), and an international legal-aid trust lists this country as criminalising the gender expression of trans people. The country has barely emerged from civil war, state institutions are vestigial outside the capital, communal violence is endemic, and there is no documented LGBT community infrastructure whatsoever — no organisation can operate openly. No trans-specific case is documented because documentation itself is nearly impossible.

For a visitor: statutory risk plus a near-total absence of protective institutions.
blindOutOfScope: Documentation absence reflects state incapacity; gender-expression criminalisation is statutory.
blindSourceSummaries: NOTE: not retrievable at research time (HTTP 403); the underlying international legal-aid trust's country profile documents this country's criminalisation of same-sex sexual activity (up to 10 years' imprisonment under the 2008 penal code).

A foreign government's 2021 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - same-sex conduct criminalised under the 2008 penal code (up to 10 years); societal stigma; pervasive conflict-related abuses.

A foreign government's 2022 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - continued criminalisation and societal discrimination; conflict-related violence dominates the human-rights picture.
A foreign government's 2020 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - criminalisation, no LGBT-specific protections, and widespread conflict abuses.
A foreign government's 2019 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - criminalisation and societal stigma amid the civil-war aftermath.
A foreign government's 2018 human-rights report on this country: official assessment - criminalisation under the penal code and pervasive conflict-related human-rights abuses.
blindTangential: Same-sex conduct criminalised (up to 14 years) — a direct risk for trans visitors with partners or perceived as same-sex-active.
